title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Resolve four quotient bits per step in the combinational divider
motivation:
The baseline ran at a median 5.442 MHz. Gowin reported a 199.837 ns path
through forwarding and the EX ALU. The single-cycle 32-bit division and
remainder operators are likely sources of that depth. They constrain the
clock even on cycles when CoreMark executes an add or a load.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU with one combinational radix-16 restoring
divider. Starting with remainder zero, consume the unsigned dividend from
the most significant nibble in eight steps. At each step append the next
nibble to the remainder and try the 15 nonzero multiples of the divisor
in parallel. The largest multiple that fits gives both the quotient digit
and the residual to carry into the next step. Eight serial digit decisions
shorten the EX path while retaining single-cycle execution and forwarding.
A scratch prototype reached 6.324, 6.907 and 6.907 MHz on Gowin placement
options 0, 1 and 2. It passed 13,588 arithmetic comparisons and validated
all CoreMark CRCs in the baseline's 4,491,485 bracketed cycles. The median
clock gives 15.38 iterations/s, a 26.9% gain over 12.12 iterations/s.

changes.description:

In step i (1 through 8), the dividend prefix bounds the trial width

tests into fit flags. Use adjacent flags to one-hot select the
residual, including the unmodified trial for digit zero. Encode
each quotient nibble from the fit flags. Select the final quotient
or remainder magnitude, then apply the quotient sign or dividend
sign as appropriate. Preserve the zero-divisor results, INT_MIN/-1
semantics, ALTOPS equations and combinational ALU interface.

Cross-check all four ops against integer truncation toward zero.
Include unsigned dividends one below, equal to, and one above each
representable digit threshold k*D for k = 1 through 15, plus high-bit
divisors, signed extrema and seeded random multi-digit quotients.

title: Move division and remainder into a shared six-round EX divider
motivation:
Gowin reports a 199.837 ns, 156-cell path through forwarding and the EX ALU.
The signed and unsigned division and remainder operators in that ALU can put
a full 32-bit division between registers. The reference ISS retired
2,922,015 instructions strictly between the timing markers for the canonical
2K, -O3, ten-iteration build. It executed 93,960 MULs and zero instructions
from the DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU group. Giving just those four operations extra
cycles should shorten the clock period with negligible measured cycle cost.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU one blocking divider in EX. Capture forwarded
operand magnitudes and sign flags on issue. Zero-extend the dividend to 36
bits and consume six bits per clock for six clocks with six cascaded binary
restoring steps. Register the partial quotient and remainder after each
group. On the following clock select and sign-correct the result into
EX/MEM. This adds seven cycles per divide with a ready bus and keeps the
ordinary ALU and multiply paths single-cycle. At the baseline's 4,491,485
marker cycles, a median Fmax above 5.70 MHz clears the acceptance margin
and 8.17 MHz delivers the forecast 50% fitness gain. Measure both because
extra cycles before the start marker can shift the pseudo-random bus stalls.

title: Predict direct control flow with 32 two-bit counters in fetch
motivation:
Fetch currently advances to PC+4 on every accepted instruction. IF/ID is
combinational, so each aligned taken branch or jump resolved in EX costs
one fetch opportunity. A replay of the canonical CoreMark instruction trace
reproduced the baseline's 4,491,485 marker cycles with the harness stall
sequence. It counted 294,425 taken conditional branches and 49,367 JALs.

hypothesis.motivation:

one fetch opportunity. A replay of the canonical CoreMark instruction trace
reproduced the baseline's 4,491,485 marker cycles with the harness stall
sequence. It counted 294,425 taken conditional branches and 49,367 JALs.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Use 32 two-bit saturating counters indexed by fetch PC[6:2]. Read the
counter in parallel with instruction memory. For a legal conditional branch
choose its PC-relative target when the high counter bit is set. For JAL
always choose its PC-relative target. Use PC+4 for other opcodes, including
JALR, and for a speculative target outside aligned instruction RAM.
Compute the target from the fetched instruction's B/J displacement.
Carry the selected direction and counter snapshot with the accepted
instruction into EX. Because the direct target is determined by those
same instruction bits, EX can detect a direction error with one bit.
Train once per valid, advancing legal conditional branch using its actual
outcome. Correct to the resolved next PC on a direction error or an aligned
JALR. Keep trap, link and RVFI next-PC decisions under EX control.
A temporary RTL prototype completed the ten-iteration CoreMark run in
4,203,476 marker cycles with all five expected CRCs. Gowin placement options
0, 1 and 2 yielded 5.165, 5.484 and 5.484 MHz. The median gives 13.05
iterations/s, 7.64% above the 12.12 baseline. At this cycle count the
implementation needs a median above 5.329 MHz to clear the acceptance
threshold. The prototype used 12,670 LUT4s against the baseline's 12,312.

title: Halve the divider's serial decisions with radix-4 restoring steps
motivation:
Gowin traced the champion's 197-cell worst path from quotient_q[35] to
remainder_q[12]. Each divider round puts six dependent trial subtractions
and remainder selections between those registers. CoreMark executed zero
divides or remainders between the markers, yet this path sets the clock
for all 4,491,485 measured cycles. At that cycle count, 45.89 MHz would
clear the acceptance margin over the champion's 43.865 MHz.

for all 4,491,485 measured cycles. At that cycle count, 45.89 MHz would

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace each pair of binary restoring steps with one radix-4 digit.
For each digit, append two dividend bits to the partial remainder and
subtract D, 2D and 3D in parallel, where D is the divisor magnitude.
Use the borrow flags to select the largest multiple that fits, its
two-bit digit, and its already-computed residual. Resolve the top two
dividend bits in round one and six bits in each of the next five rounds.
Keep the current six-round protocol in hardware and ALTOPS.

A scratch RTL prototype reached 46.988, 47.706 and 47.706 MHz on Gowin
placement options 0, 1 and 2. CoreMark validated all five CRCs in
4,491,485 bracketed cycles for ten iterations. The measured median gives
106.21 iterations/s, 8.76% above the 97.66 champion. Option 0 used
3,048 LUT4s against the champion's 2,756. All three worst paths now
start at the register file.

title: Split the six-round divider by divisor magnitude
motivation:
Gowin traced the champion's 197-cell setup path from quotient_q[35] to
remainder_q[12] through six dependent 33-bit restoring steps. This limits
all instructions to a median 43.865 MHz, even though CoreMark retired zero
divides or remainders in its 4,491,485 marker cycles.

divides or remainders in its 4,491,485 marker cycles.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Use two unsigned restoring datapaths under the existing six-round controller.
Let A and D be the 32-bit operand magnitudes. For 0 < D < 2^14, every
restored remainder fits in 14 bits. This lane can consume six dividend bits
per clock with 15-bit trial subtractors. For D >= 2^14, the top 14 bits of A
already form a valid remainder smaller than D. Seed the wide lane with that
prefix and consume the remaining 18 bits in six groups of three. Only three
33-bit subtractors lie in series on this lane. Both lanes advance together.
One bit captured at issue selects the result after the final round.

A scratch prototype reached 43.834, 47.203 and 47.203 MHz on Gowin placement
options 0, 1 and 2. It used 2,839 LUT4s against the champion's 2,756.
CoreMark validated all five CRCs in 4,491,485 marker cycles with both bus
stalls enabled. The median gives 105.09 iterations/s, 7.61% above 97.66.
The reported option-0 worst path moved to the register-file, EX redirect
and ID hazard logic. The implementation needs a median above 45.882 MHz
at this cycle count to clear the acceptance margin.

dividend bits MSB first. Keep digit calculation local to each lane.

reconstructs A in the remainder. Fill the upper 14 quotient bits

correction after selecting the magnitude. Preserve the six-round

title: Serve recurring control transfers from a 64-entry branch target buffer
motivation:
The champion spends 4,491,485 marker cycles per ten CoreMark iterations.
An aligned taken transfer discards one fetch opportunity when EX resolves it,
and a recurring branch still waits for imem even after its direction is
predictable. The previous 32-counter predictor saved 6.4% of cycles on
the original core. On the champion, a scratch implementation of that design
ran in 4,203,401 cycles at 41.304 MHz, below the tournament cutoff.

the original core. On the champion, a scratch implementation of that design

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give each entry of a 64-entry, direct-mapped branch target buffer (BTB)
its source instruction word as well as a tag, resolved target and two-bit
counter. A tag hit can supply both the control transfer during an imem wait

even when its counter predicts fall-through. Only resolved conditional
branches, JALs and JALRs can populate the buffer.

With instruction replay disabled, the prototype took 4,197,517 marker
cycles. Serving the saved branch word on a hit reduced that to 4,043,251
with all five expected CRCs. Gowin placement options 0, 1 and 2 reached
43.124, 43.014 and 43.014 MHz. The median gives 106.38 iterations/s,
8.9% above the champion. The design needs 41.303 MHz at this cycle count
to clear the 4.6% cutoff. Placement option 0 used 3,015 LUT4s and 8 BSRAMs.
The prototype passed all 53 single-retire formal checks and matched the
reference retirement trace on selftest and all three random programs with
both memory stall generators enabled.

title: Shorten the champion's divider feedback path with radix-4 digits
motivation:
On the current BTB-equipped core, Gowin traced a 28.668 ns path from
remainder_q to quotient_q through six dependent restoring steps. That
path limits the clock on all 4,043,251 CoreMark marker cycles. The
earlier radix-4 experiment reached 47.652 MHz on the pre-BTB core.
At the champion's cycle count, a median above 45.40 MHz would clear
the 4.6% acceptance margin.

motivation:

title: Replay the instruction sequence on each predicted branch path
motivation:
The champion took 4,043,251 marker cycles. Replaying the branch instruction
on a branch target buffer (BTB) hit saved 154,266 cycles in the previous experiment.
The BTB predicts where execution continues, but fetch still waits for imem
on the ordinary instructions along that path. Repeated loop backedges and
calls give the predictor several consecutive fetches it can anticipate.

remainder together. MEM can then complete the two low bits and restore the
sign directly from these registers.

title: Predict the effective-address carry to replay loads during RAM waits
motivation:
A marker-bracketed trace of the champion counted 191,317 data-bus stall
cycles, 45,890 redirects and 19,787 cycles without a fetch word over ten
CoreMark iterations. The 544,852 loads give a word-address predictor a
larger opportunity than further improvements to branch direction. A
PC-stride load predictor saved only 39,881 cycles in a scratch run.

raw words observed on the data bus and their address tags.

carry to select either upper-slice sum. Give these bits their own

ordinary-RAM range, natural alignment and write-collision status. An
accepted bus read supplies the live word. During backpressure a
verified prediction can supply the same word and complete the load.

register identifier through EX forwarding and the ALU to data RAM.

motivation:

title: Predict a counted loop's exit when writing its next replay successor
motivation:
Between the timing markers the champion resolves 529,588 conditional
branches and redirects on 43,919 of them. Two branches each produce
3,241 redirects in 29,160 visits. Each repeats eight taken outcomes
followed by one exit. A two-bit counter quickly learns the backedge
but misses nearly every exit. The replay RAM already has a place to
store the predicted successor for a branch's next visit.

outcomes, including ordinary bimodal increments and decrements. When a
legal, cacheable conditional branch advances in EX, its actual
direction selects exactly one training transaction. After the final
expected continuation, write fall-through for a backward branch or
the target for a forward branch into the normal replay row. After
the observed exit, write the continuation for the next invocation.

every other fill use the existing counter. Fetch can follow the
stored link at the existing latency.

title: Finish ordered comparisons across the existing EX/MEM register
motivation:
In the champion's Gowin placement 0, bit 2 of the forwarded EX/MEM result
feeds a 37-cell path through rs2 to the decode flush. In placement 1 an
operand-to-fetch recovery path is within 0.001 ns of the longest path.
CoreMark executes 166,519 ordered branches and set-less-than instructions
in the timing window. None of the 14,667 set-less-than results had an
immediately following instruction naming its destination as a source.
Adding an EX wait to every comparison would spend
more cycles than the champion currently loses to all pipeline bubbles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Pipeline the magnitude comparator for BLT, BGE, BLTU, BGEU, SLT, SLTU,
SLTI and SLTIU at the existing EX/MEM boundary. Compare bits 31:16 and

for signed order. At the edge capture upper-less, upper-equal and
lower-less. In MEM the exact less-than bit is upper-less OR
(upper-equal AND lower-less). A set-less-than writes that bit zero-extended
on the existing late-result path. An immediately dependent consumer uses
the same one-bubble interlock as MULH.

An ordered branch can accept its predicted successor into EX. Register
the direct target, fall-through PC and the two correction decisions with
the comparison. Fold BGE polarity into those decisions in collection so
MEM selects directly on less-than. A correction has priority over younger
redirects, annuls the younger EX transfer and fetch/decode work, and
suppresses younger divider issue and replay training on that edge. Train
the older branch exactly once using its registered fetch snapshot. Handle
a taken misaligned target as a trap continuing at PC+4. BEQ and BNE
retain their current EX timing.

A functional prototype retired ten validated CoreMark iterations in
3,063,914 marker cycles with both stall generators, 19,605 cycles above
the champion (0.64%). At that count the qualifying median is above
102.389 MHz. Keep the late correction local to valid and side-effect
controls and feed the registered recovery PCs directly into fetch. The
frequency gain depends on the remaining integer ALU and load-return paths.

title: Split shift execution across EX and MEM with a direct byte-shift path
motivation:
In the champion's 97.260 MHz placement, the path from the EX operand-B
select to integer result bit 9 arrives at 15.578 ns, within 0.002 ns
of the worst path. The five distance bits currently control a full
barrel shift before its result joins the shared EX/MEM bypass word.
Moving the byte-distance portion across that register can shorten EX.
CoreMark frequently needs an immediately dependent shift result, so
the choice of shifts that complete in one cycle determines the cost.

hypothesis.motivation:

CoreMark frequently needs an immediately dependent shift result, so

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Execute SLL, SRL and SRA in two parts. EX performs the shift by bits
2 through 0 of the resolved distance. MEM can shift that registered
partial result by 0, 8, 16 or 24 more bits. Both stages use the same
direction and arithmetic-right sign fill. For immediate distances
8, 16 and 24, decode the complete shift in collection and wire the
displaced bytes directly into the EX result. Distances below eight
already finish in EX. All five RV32 distance bits remain significant
for register shifts regardless of how rs2 was forwarded.

Predecode the direction and byte distance together into enables for
the fixed byte routes. Suppress the fine shifter's result select
during collection for those immediate forms. This keeps a late
direction or byte-route mux off the common integer result. Give the
fine shifter its own three-bit distance input so the other ALU
functions still receive the original full-width operands.

Carry a needs-completion bit and coarse shift controls beside the
EX/MEM partial word. MEM supplies the exact result to WB and older
writer forwarding. An independent successor advances immediately.
If an adjacent consumer selected an unfinished shift, use the existing
load-repair hold to replace only its matching source or sources before
it can execute, redirect, start division or access memory. Hold all
shift metadata with its producer on backpressure. Keep load verification
and this completion condition distinct.

MEM took 3,082,664 marker cycles. Adding the three direct immediate
distances reduced that to 3,044,495, only 186 cycles above the champion.

CRCs and the validation banner. The fully predecoded byte routes also
matched the 3,044,495-cycle result. The fine-only EX prototype without
the three byte routes reached 91.488 MHz on placement 1. At the final
cycle count promotion requires
a median above 101.74 MHz. The timing hypothesis is that collection
can absorb the full route decode and shorten the EX result path enough
to reach that clock.

title: Steer fetch with a four-bit PC match and verify replay words separately
motivation:
The champion retires 2,922,016 instructions in 3,044,309 CoreMark marker
cycles. Even perfect issue at 97.260 MHz would gain only 4.19%, below
the 4.6% promotion margin. Today a taken prediction waits for the
replay row's full PC comparison and the dynamic selection of one of
sixteen initialized bits. Fetch needs both checks to issue a cached
instruction. EX can recover a speculative target using the existing
direction and target checks.

instruction data and reporting prediction.hit. This lets a ready

checked. A buffered, previously verified word can supply its hint
directly. Snapshot the actual taken bit and target in the usual
prediction bundle, including on a partial match that misses the full
tag, so EX can recover at the existing misprediction latency.

Register it with the replay row and its index, hold all three together
during buffering, and retain live_q's collision and invalidation

hint. On a ready response, retain the external opcode check. A stalled
imem can issue only a verified replay word. Aliasing can change the

above 101.738 MHz. The remaining uncertainty is whether shortening
fetch steering improves the clock before an independent EX path limits it.
